title: Avoid loading the author when checking post ownership
bug: Authors get 403 when editing their own posts.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The diff changes the ownership check from comparing the loaded author object to comparing the user_id directly, but token_auth.current_user() returns a User object, not an ID, causing a type mismatch that incorrectly denies access to the legitimate author.

doppel_guided.summary: The PR introduces a regression where legitimate authors receive 403 Forbidden because the code compares a User object to an integer ID.

suspicions.claim: The ownership check compares post.user_id (int) to token_auth.current_user() (User object), which will always be False, allowing any authenticated user to edit any post.
suspicions.trigger: 1. Create user A and user B. 2. Log in as user A and create a post (note its id). 3. Log in as user B. 4. PUT /api/posts/<id> with JSON {"text": "hacked"} and user B's Bearer token. 5. Observe 200 response and the post text changed. 6. GET /api/posts/<id> to confirm the edit persisted.
suspicions.evidence: Probe probe_s1_ownership sent PUT /api/posts/1 with user B's token and both base and head answered 403, showing the ownership check blocks the edit.
